steps.text: 'Terra', 'the land', 'these lands', the nations 'across the world'.
These terms and the language around them flow in widespread use only because of how narrow they actually are.

Has there ever been some majestic language of the ancient past that could describe everything between heaven and earth? Where we put into words the 'everything' we might encounter in our day-to-day lives?
A grandiose term encompassing the earth, the sky, and even the seas of which the landbound nations know so little? A single word to narrate millennia of life's progress?
Where among the collective mind of mankind is such a word, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm sure you know the answer yourself.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: I know quite a bit myself, yet still I find myself asking, day after day. No man may truly escape the unknown, and the unknown will forever torment mankind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) 'Alma.' 'World.'

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Hm. And here I thought you would go with the Sargonian word 'Alam'. The same idea, I think.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Yours was a Sarkaz language?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Strange. You're a Feline who calls herself a doctor, yet your first instinct is to use the devils' tongue.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Your identity is like the ever-changing clouds above the sea. Never content to remain the same.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Language will not change its essence for such trifles.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Language, hmm... Now look here, Kal'tsit. A well.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Do you know how to draw water from it? Do you know how the Iberians used these blue cornerstones to build their houses?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If the Iberian nobility hadn't let their pride go to their heads, the ocean would surely have made the nation an impenetrable fortress.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The well is deep, and we're very close to the shore.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Look. It hasn't yet dried up. There is a false sun inside.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We should be on our way, sir.
The elderly man does not answer her. He simply picks up a small rock in silence.

The rock could not be more commonplace, with no particular reason to fiddle with. Yet, as though absorbed in the sensation of the sea breeze on his skin, he continues to gaze at the bottom of the well.
Kal'tsit doesn't push the issue. She silently waits for the man in front of her to answer. She sees that the clouds are moving. The winds are strong.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: There is no rush, Kal'tsit. There is no rush. We have ample time for rest... no matter the arrangements you've made.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: If I dropped this rock into the well, how long would it take for us to hear the splash?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: About five to six seconds.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Even the most simple Iberian knows how to make use of the sea. Knowledge that went into this deep coastal well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And yet, a Victorian farmer or Columbian worker might not even know what the vast sea looks like.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Hmm... Kal'tsit, how many questions have I asked you on our journey so far?
The old man holds his arm out, the rock still in his palm. Then he lets go, sending it tumbling downward.
Despite its rapid descent, the two of them lock their eyes onto it. Yet without adequate sunlight, they soon find themselves unable to follow its trek into the depths.
It has been two, perhaps three seconds. Nothing but silence shrouds the two of them. Even the wind has come to a halt.
How quiet, Kal'tsit thinks to herself. How quiet indeed.
*Plop*
The quiet sound echoes through the well's walls, as though reminding them that, in that brief moment lasting but a few seconds, all the lands are still.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: One hundred twenty-three. Quite a bewitching number.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: One hundred twenty-three questions, over one hundred twenty-three years. The Inquisition boasts not a single Inquisitor older than me.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Most have died in battle, a few of old age, and even fewer gave in to cowardice during their endless ordeal. It did not end very well for them.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: I've experienced all there is of Iberia. I've seen its fleets setting sail, and heard the Victorian envoys quivering.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: It was a rude awakening when the Profound Silence destroyed our nation. My countrymen are still drowning in their hatred for the disaster, and confused over the loss of their dream.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Liberi don't live long lives. Even the Liberi Elders, the oldest and healthiest of them, are unable to shoulder Iberia's present calamity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your age is a miracle. One forged by the Inquisition, and which also grants you an unprecedented sense of devotion.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In that era, when both glory and ideology began to crumble, you and the earliest Inquisition members were revered as 'Saints.'

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: 'Saints.' A title for those who once served as a guiding beacon for mankind. But just like firewood, it's become nothing but ashes.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: I've watched the seasons cycle by a full hundred and twenty-three times, yet it seems only the cold winters have left their mark on me. I've seen so many truths with my own eyes, yet can never recall the sight of spring.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes?
The look in the old man's eyes changes.
Faith is a language, and prayers can pave roads. At this very moment, the nation of Iberia, or perhaps an existence beyond that, is caressing its chin, examining the wind speed.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: So far, I've lived one hundred twenty-three years. I've asked you one hundred twenty-three questions, based on my personal experiences.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Nonetheless, you answered each and every one. You know everything that I know.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Man is making progress, and new secrets will forever emerge, yet our knowledge will never be able to overcome that wall we call 'the known.'

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Regardless, the enemy we face belongs to the other side of that wall, in the dark forest that lies beyond.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: And you, Kal'tsit. Do you belong to our side of the wall... or to the depths of that forest?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That is up to you.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Hoh... You might even know the number of leaves on its trees. What a terrifying woman.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Make no mistake, the saints of Iberia remain the pinnacle that humanity can reach. Yet you've exceeded that, marking you as inhuman.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Perhaps you've extended your life with special Arts, perhaps you've inherited some kind of ancient identity, or perhaps you possess a soul that had great ambitions.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Even if our faith is only a lie built atop ideology, we nevertheless once held onto it firmly. What is truly saddening, though, is that when old age finally bests us all, we will have not yet managed to solve our problems.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: While those of us who have bested old age—via Originium Arts or other means—will only come to fear endless suffering at the hands of our enemies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When did Ægir become such an unknown terror to Iberia?

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: How could an unarmed child so easily accept the help of a stranger brandishing a weapon?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What if that child were about to drown?

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Then we would still require proof. Is Ægir's current situation really as you say? Can the Seaborn and their source truly be defeated?

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: If you cannot back up these claims, then Iberia will not trust you. I will not trust you.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Before I die, you... you must all prove it to Iberia.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Otherwise, the seawater will quench the flame of civilization. Before the other nations can prepare, they will swarm past Iberia... and tear this 'world' apart.

steps.name: Prudent Elder
steps.text: Perhaps this too—the refutation of Terran civilization—is itself a part of their survival-of-the-fittest mindset.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Or perhaps there is nothing inherently different between us and them.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: A seaside town, huh? Relaxed, but gloomy. Quiet, but bustling. A lively place, but with danger and mystery around every corner.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Just the place to get us in that creative groove!

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: What do you girls say?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs lightheartedly)

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: The shore's got an unsettling vibe. I can already smell all that stuff I'd rather not.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I really don't think we should be visiting the waterfront so carelessly.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Does it matter, if we can find inspiration? C'mon, look how fired up about it Dan is.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs depressingly)

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Time to find our muse!

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Right... It's a good chance.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I can't believe we're actually looking to that messed up ocean for inspiration now.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Yeah, which is exactly why it's a fresh new vibe!

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Took the words outta my mouth.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs in agreement)

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Well, should we split up, then? I can take our luggage to the hotel on my own.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Alright! I'll be checking stuff out over there.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: All by yourself?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I'm glad SOMEONE's worrying. Just don't forget we're playing with fire here.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: So where's the hotel?

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: That reminds me, how did a small town like this get itself a hotel anyway? Do people even come here?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: They need to make a living somehow.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Right. No living, no music.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs)

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: The sea...

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: We're back.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Excuse me... can I get past?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh, sure, no problem.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Have you been sitting in the chapel again, Mr... uhh...?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Elysium.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry... We've even run into each other several times already.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Don't worry about it. The name 'Elysium' isn't very common here.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Actually, someone as smoking hot as me has gotta be a rare sight in Iberia to begin with, right?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't know about that... but someone as confident as you, maybe.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: It took spending some time here to realize that the place that I always called home doesn't really feel like home.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are you still waiting for someone here, Mr. Elysium? It's already been several days, hasn't it?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Haha, not like I have a choice. That's just how things are in my line of work. Besides, I'd rather hang out in comfort here than that in primeval forest infested with bugs and Originium.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You're from outside then?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh, you can tell? Is it because of the vibe I give off?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Actually... uh... I guess you could say that?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Like... the way you dress?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You know your stuff.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Gran Faro doesn't see a lot of visitors... There's not a lot of folks here, so everyone in town knows everyone else.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Besides... What with how close to the sea we are, not a lot of Liberi are willing to talk to Ægir these days.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Especially after the Inquisition started showing up more often.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I get you. I've been through similar stuff plenty of times.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Does this happen in other Iberian cities, too? Like in those prosperous ones I hear about in the rumors?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Not just in Iberia, kid. The way I see it, it's pretty much the same no matter where you go. Life's tough everywhere.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But I gotta say, some of the Ægirs I've met are a real handful. Just thinking about 'em gives me a headache. Wish I could beam all my common sense straight into their brains.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Which makes you pretty easy to get along with, by comparison.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Okay, now THAT's a face asking who'd ever want the common sense of a guy like me.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: N-No it's not!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Sure, I look like an unemployed bum lazing about here 24-7, but I've actually come a loooong way and been through waaaaay too much.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So... you're an explorer, then? What's life like for the Ægir in other places?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Not too bad.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Not too bad...
Mayor Thiago... You needn't come here every day.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I've been hearing some bad rumors lately. I'm worried about you guys, Amaia.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Bad rumors... You mean about the cultists?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: But we're not just close to the sea, we're close to the Inquisition too, and the very heart of Iberia.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: So how could there possibly be cultists here?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Who knows? Happens all the time in coastal towns though. Hardly peculiar at all.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Also... I heard someone saw a monster on the shore.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Did Old Pedri tell you that?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You know the kind of nonsense he goes on about when he hasn't had his drink.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You're a kind man, Thiago. I'm sure you're just worried about Jordi, the boy who works at the chapel.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I... I'm not a very sophisticated one though. Maybe you can put me at ease... help me sleep better at night.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: These rumors are just rumors, right? The ghost ship, the cultists, the sea monsters?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The Inquisition hasn't let us go out to sea in a long, long time.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Right. Can't even remember how long... Eighty-four years? Eighty-five?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Try fifty or sixty. The Profound Silence happened in 1038.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Have you really been trapped on land for so long, in your memories? You aren't even that old. Have you been a prisoner of this place since before you were born?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: If living in poverty counts as imprisonment, then yes, I've been a prisoner for a long, long time.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I haven't so much as looked at the sea since Marin died. I loathe it.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: But you're not worried about the gossip, are you? You're worried about the Inquisition. And even more so about the Penal Battalion coming here to take away all the Ægirs.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: *Sigh*, poor Thiago...

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The Inquisition snuffed out the love of your life, an Ægir woman. Your anger and resentment is perfectly understandable, but be careful what you say. For everyone's sake.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...Maybe you're right.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Okay, I'll be careful. You always know more than the rest of us, anyway. So what've you been up to lately?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The same old. Doing my job as a third-rate translator in this frighteningly laidback seaside town.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: That said, it's been months since a Messenger stopped by. All my drafts have been piling up, and it's giving me a headache.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: *Sigh*... Translation! I've never even set foot outside this small town my whole life. Anything besides Iberian may as well be gibberish to me.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Hm, it's getting late.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Right, Jordi should be off work soon. I only hope that the Inquisition isn't gonna give the lad any trouble over that gossip, these next few days.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I'll see you later.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Be safe, Mayor Thiago.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: ...Cultists. Hm.
The young woman named Amaia ponders for a moment before turning her mind back to the papers, as always.
Ursine novels, Kazimierzian biographies, Leithanian poetry... even Sargonian folk tales.
All the lands of Terra lie before her as a thick pile of literature, each word waiting to be deciphered in a solemn, orderly manner.
The air is extraordinarily humid. She can't help but pinch the corner of the page.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The sensation of the sea...

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: 'The waves continue to accelerate, and the winds are frightened. The corals line the sky, painting it a neon shade.'

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: 'We will come to detest ourselves for not having wings.'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Are you finished with your work?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, uh... yes.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: As you can see, the chapel doesn't see a lot of visitors. I mostly just keep the place tidy.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are you still waiting today?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Yeah. They should've been here by last week, but my superior did warn me that they're a weird bunch. So I guess being late is normal enough.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Still, it's hard to call that a good thing. But why would anyone choose to meet up in Gran Faro of all places?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Strange, right? I thought so, too. That's why I volunteered for the job when Misery brought it up.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Not that I expected to waste a whole month here. That's a hell of a long time to be on standby.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But... normally the Inquisition wouldn't have let outsiders like you in at all.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Because of how close it is to their command center?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Or... because it's close to the sea?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Maybe both.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So how did you make it here? I haven't traveled much, but even I can tell that Gran Faro is a backwater...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: If you really wanna know, I could use someone to chat with. I'm dying of boredom over here.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Then if it's not too much trouble— Oh!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't realize it was so late. Uncle Thiago is waiting. I should head back to make dinner.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Family?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uh... Something like that. He's the one who raised me.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Look, you don't have to be such a doormat just because you're an Ægir. When someone's kind to you, try to be more positive.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uh, thanks... Mr. Elysium.
Gran Faro. It means 'the great lighthouse' in an ancient Iberian tongue.
Lighthouses once shone upon ships both large and small, and served as homes for all seamen to return to.
Many souls dwelled beneath the reefs, until the ships fell in love with the ocean, accepting its embrace and facing their own destruction.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (Amaia? Where is she going... Hm?)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (Some sort of commotion up ahead? That's unusual. What's going on?)

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Where are you heading?

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: The chapel! Peeps here shouldn't be using their hands to pray, they should learn to drum instead!

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: This square is the center of the town. Everything's built around it.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A sculpture of a lighthouse.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A guiding landmark to the sea... and the town.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: What a lame analogy!

steps.name: Passing Townsperson
steps.text: What a bunch of weirdos. Let's not get too close.

steps.name: Spectating Townsperson
steps.text: Didn't Old Pedri mention something like this before?

steps.name: Passing Townsperson
steps.text: Don't get involved, lest the Inquisition take you away.

steps.name: Passing Townsperson
steps.text: Sheesh, why are there all these outsiders lately? The Inquisition just doesn't care anymore, huh?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (I haven't seen any of them before... Look at the way they're dressed... Are they musicians?)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: (Er, is she looking at me?)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: H-Hello?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: In the past, I wouldn't have batted an eye at seeing an Ægir near the coast, but it sure is a rare sight these days.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Do you know what's going on here?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: W-What?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Oh, you wouldn't, huh? You aren't a child of the sea. You're land-born.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: *Sigh*... Not that that's much of a surprise. Jeez.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Aya, over here!

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Coming!

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Oh, right... you... hmm...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I-Is something the matter?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Do you know what that sculpture is of? And do all the locals know?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yes... It's a lighthouse. Apparently, they needed a lot of people to work on it way back when, and many of the workers' families ended up staying here.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Like yours?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uh... Yes. I still keep some relics from that era back home. Like, blueprints and pictures.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Yep... lighthouses. Iberian lighthouses. In a country on the land. That's kinda funny.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Anyway, the scent doesn't seem to be coming from you. Alright, then, you be extra careful.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I've never seen those people... Are those instruments?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Maybe they're the ones Mr. Elysium has been waiting for?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Jordi.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, Uncle Thiago. Sorry. I should've come back sooner—

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't you get involved with them. I didn't see ears OR tails, and no feathers either. They might be Ægirs.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Jordi, my boy. You know I don't have anything against the Ægir, but remember what everyone's been saying lately.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't get too involved with these outsiders. If you see an Ægir near the sea and there's no one from the Inquisition or Penal Battalion around, then they gotta be trouble.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: I don't think they're bad people, but the Inquisition might not see things the same way, so... I'm sorry. I just don't want to see them take you away. Be a good boy and listen.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I get it. You don't have to apologize.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I get it...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I didn't expect you to agree so quickly.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I know of the events in Sal Viento, with the three Abyssal Hunters. Irene always writes the most detailed reports, after all.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: And above all, I know that if you meant Iberia harm, you had other, much simpler options.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Abyssal Hunters... Suppose they are as strong and swift as the report suggests. The three of them are still controllable by the Inquisition.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We retain the authority to sentence them to death. The only reason they are still allowed to walk Iberian lands is thanks to my curiosity towards your so-called truth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can't help but wonder if Iberia's current predicament is a result of its pride, then.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The truth is that no one knows pride better than us. Pride is like the shadow always lurking behind every man.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The two inquisitors with whom you're acquainted have already received orders. Should the need arise, they will appear before us.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: It seems we have a few unidentified Ægirs in Gran Faro as well. You never mentioned them.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Who are they?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They aren't Ægir.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Iberia is rarely mentioned in the historical record, but that doesn’t mean our history is short. At the height of our prosperity, we crossed the entire continent, advancing troops to even Bolívar.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Both coin and knowledge flooded into our cities like streams pouring into a valley from a high cliff. Those glorious waterfalls roared so deafeningly loud that they could overcome even the waves of the sea.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: (Sargonian) Those beings that arose... or rather, the 'Feranmut.'

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Perhaps it is them that I should keep an eye on. They show no signs of hostility, yet they keep me on edge... Maybe they once belonged to the sea.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Kal'tsit, you are the doctor here. Could you do the Inquisition a favor?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Ask away.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Inquisition's command center is very close to the coastline. We are prepared to face destruction at any moment.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But I need you, an outsider, to be our eyes, gazing forward.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Seeing as we're in the same boat, I have no reason to refuse.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Please, Doctor, spare me the mysteriousness your long life has earned you. Show us where the evil that lurks within us sleeps.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll take that as a compliment... and it would be my honor.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Gladiia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Our brief time together has you addressing me differently. On that point alone, you are quite different from before.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain, I have a question.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We've already shared all the information we have, in the time since we left that reeking coast.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Not all of it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: We alone are more than enough. I don't understand why we must also bring—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Look at her now. This is how she once was.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I looked into all her treatment records at Rhodes Island... You've never seen her this quiet before either, have you?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Don't you want to help her?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And this will help?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: She alone can defeat her illusions. She is her own key. She can break through the results of those filthy experiments. She's Laurentina, after all.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But until then, we need to prepare a warm bed for her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It was only for a short while, but she woke up... Even so, I stared at her like that.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Don't be so sentimental. We aren't her. If she doesn't mind the way she is, we have no right to meddle in it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You trust Dr. Kal'tsit more than I thought you would.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Maybe. She willingly stayed in Iberia and created this opportunity for us. I was surprised. And I have to thank her.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I can only hope it all goes well for her.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Look at the time.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Guess it's not happening today either. And here I thought I'd get to see them sooner or later just by waiting in the most conspicuous building in town.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: This really is such an uneventful place, though. If I'd known it'd be so boring here, I would've brought along a few more books from Rhodes Island—

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: —A Lateran chapel! And in such a great shape, even right next to the sea! Unbelievable! This place's style really has a different vibe, though.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: I mean, as long as there are Laterans in chapels, we can jam whenever, but this place just feels so gloomy... Hm?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Ahh—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: —Alty?!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You'd best stay away from the sea, Jordi. The chapel is clean and safe. Just stay there.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't worry about anything else. Not a lot of the young ones came back this year. Most who left looked for ways to move to the big cities. And now we rely on the Inquisition's handouts to get by.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: You should think about what I said and leave this place. The folks here are the families of the workmen who gathered here to maintain the lighthouse in the past, but times have changed. This place will be abandoned sooner or later.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Jordi?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm listening, Uncle.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's just... where can an Ægir go?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Amaia told me that there are places outside, in other parts of Iberia, where they aren't so harsh on the Ægir.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I'll need to find a home for myself eventually. I need resources, connections. I... can't make a decision that easily.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I'm not ready yet.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...If you say so.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Right, Amaia gave me another book, one she translated herself. Not like I'd understand it anyway, though. Take it with you to kill time over in the chapel.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Okay.
Jordi walks down the street quietly.
Seeing the old man in front of him hunching over more and more, he can't help but think back to how he looked just last year.
As if to prove how time slowly overtakes us all, senility is always silent. From the moment you wake up to when you fall asleep, every second is like a gasp for air.
But Jordi never complained. He's used to this life, after all.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm pretty happy with my life right now. I get to help out at the chapel. Sometimes I help take care of the children, and sometimes I help patch up the injured workmen.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I even got to know that Liberi who came from out of town the other day. He's so different from everyone else. He said his name is Elysium. You don't have to worry about me.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's been a long time since the Inquisition came to town. We don't always have to be so nervous.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: That's not a chapel, lad. It's a sentry post. The Inquisition set it up to keep their eyes on us, back when we were still trying to repair the lighthouse.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: But now that the coastline is peaceful and the work on the Eye of Iberia is shelved, of course the Inquisition doesn't give a toss about us anymore.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Still, to be fair, the Inquisition isn't completely useless. Only they can stop those...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Those...?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Nothing, lad. Just a few rumors going around among the workmen.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Rumors, hm...

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Lad?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: H-Here...?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What exactly is that...? Should I let Uncle Thiago know...?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Something bothering you, lad?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No, it's nothing.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Uncle... Just what is there out at sea?
